newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot gas prices slide with mild temperatures.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot gas prices slide with mild temperatures.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices sharply extended last week's losses Tuesday, as the market was still plagued by mild temperatures across most of the U.S., industry sources said.

Louisiana Gulf Coast prices fell another 30 cents to the $1.70s and $1.80s per million British thermal units, down more than a $1 from February indices. Prices were lifted late by a rebound in the futures market.
March Hub gas futures traded early at $1.85, but by late morning the contract had reached a high of $1.945, just 2.1 cents shy of Friday's settlement.
In west Texas, Permian prices also softened by another 20 cents to the low-$1.60s, ladened by above-normal temperatures and ample gas storage and hydroelectric supplies in the West.
At the southern California border, prices slipped 10 cents to the high-$1.60s.
In the Midcontinent, prices were down nearly 30 cents to the $1.60-1.65 range, indicating a decline of about 70 cents from week-ago levels.
In the East, New York city-gate prices plummeted into the $2.10-2.20 range, down an average of 40 cents from Friday.
Temperatures throughout most of the U.S. are forecast to remain above normal through Friday, but a cool front is expected to push temperatures to near-normal levels by the weekend.
